entries.name: The Ontario Caregiver Organization (OCO)
entries.description: A provincial organization that offers free support to unpaid family caregivers in Ontario, including parents and family members caring for an autistic person or someone with a developmental disability. It runs the Ontario Caregiver Helpline by phone and chat, one-to-one caregiver coaching by phone or Zoom, peer support and e-learning courses.
entries.cost_note: The site describes OCO's programs and supports for caregivers as free.
entries.evidence: For information about resources and support for caregivers in your area, call the Ontario Caregiver Helpline: 1-833-416-2273.
entries.notes: Serves caregivers of people with any condition across Ontario, not only neurodivergent family members; the autism and developmental disability pages point to further supports. Caregiver coaching (up to six sessions) is eligibility-based and starts with a self-referral form.

entries.name: Caregivers Nova Scotia
entries.description: A Nova Scotia charity for unpaid family and friend caregivers, open to all caregivers whatever the age or health condition of the person they care for, so parents of autistic or other neurodivergent children and adults can use it. Regional coordinators give one-to-one support by phone or email, and it hosts more than 20 free peer support groups a month in person, by phone and online.
entries.cost_note: Support group sessions are free and open to all caregivers.
entries.evidence: Every month, we host over 20+ peer support groups with other unpaid family and friend caregivers just like you.
entries.notes: Province-wide, with regional coordinators for the Capital, Cape Breton, Northern and Eastern Mainland, Valley and Western regions, plus French-language, telephone and virtual groups. Not specific to neurodivergence; facilitators are caregivers, not clinicians.

entries.name: Family Caregivers of British Columbia (FCBC)
entries.description: A BC non-profit for anyone caring for a family member or friend, which includes parents of neurodivergent children and adults. It offers a toll-free Caregiver Support Line, one-on-one emotional support and caregiver coaching, help navigating the health care system, and monthly caregiver support groups online and in the Victoria area.
entries.cost_note: Educational resources are described as free; no fees are listed for the support line or groups.
entries.evidence: FCBC offers direct support through one-on-one emotional support, caregiver support groups, health care system navigation, and free educational resources.
entries.notes: Serves caregivers of any condition and many groups focus on elder care; the virtual groups are open province-wide. Its Other Community Supports page lists caregiver programs in other BC regions.

entries.name: Caregivers Alberta
entries.description: An Alberta charity that supports unpaid family caregivers, including parents caring for a child with autism, a developmental or cognitive disability, anxiety or other conditions. It offers one-on-one caregiver coaching by phone or email, an online Caregiver Support Community group, the COMPASS for Caregivers program and educational workshops.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed on the pages checked.
entries.evidence: Providing care for a child with disabilities or a serious illness can be both stressful and overwhelming to caregivers. This is why Caregivers Alberta is here to support you.
entries.notes: Province-wide, with its office in Edmonton. Serves caregivers of people with any condition; coaching appointments are booked by phone or email.

entries.name: Caregiver Support Helpline (L'Appui pour les proches aidants)
entries.description: A free, confidential helpline for caregivers (proches aidants) in Quebec and their families, open to anyone caring for a loved one, including parents of a neurodivergent child or adult. Trained caregiver counsellors offer listening, information and referrals by phone or live chat.
entries.cost_note: Described as a professional, confidential and free service.
entries.evidence: Caregiver Support Helpline is a professional, confidential and free service, available Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., by telephone at 1 855 852-7784, and by live chat.
entries.notes: Open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Serves caregivers of people with any condition; L'Appui also helps find local caregiver services in Quebec.

entries.name: Family Support Institute of BC (FSI)
entries.description: A BC non-profit that offers free family-to-family support for families who have a family member with a disability, including parents of neurodivergent children and adults. Families are matched with trained volunteer Resource Parents/Peers who have their own lived experience and can listen, share community resources and help with navigating services; FSI also runs workshops and free interpretation for multilingual families.
entries.cost_note: Describes its family-to-family support network and interpretation services as free.
entries.evidence: The Family Support Institute of BC (FSI) supports families who have a family member with a disability by connecting them to our provincial network of volunteers—Resource Parents/Peers (RPs).
entries.notes: Province-wide; FSI staff match families with a Resource Parent/Peer by age, region, diagnosis and experience. FSI does not act as a case manager or clinician.

entries.name: Individual & Family Advocacy (Inclusion Alberta)
entries.description: Province-wide advocates who help families of children and adults with intellectual disabilities in Alberta find and negotiate the supports they need, so families don't have to navigate complex systems alone. They help with inclusive education, family support, recreation, housing, funding and individualized planning.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.evidence: Our advocates help individuals and families address a broad range of issues including inclusive education, family support, recreation and leisure, housing, funding, individualized planning, and more.
entries.notes: Offices in Edmonton and Calgary; families contact Inclusion Alberta to ask about advocacy. The focus is intellectual disability.

entries.name: Family Support Groups (Kerry's Place)
entries.description: Topic-based support groups where parents and family members of autistic children and youth in Ontario share successes, talk through challenges and learn from each other, on topics such as going back to school, bullying and supporting rainbow families.
entries.cost_note: A Foundational Family Service, at no cost for families with children under 18 registered with the Ontario Autism Program.
entries.evidence: These family support groups use topic-focused conversations and provide caregivers the opportunity to share successes, discuss challenges, and gain insight from other parents and family members of Autistic children and youth.
entries.notes: Families register with Kerry's Place intake first; current sessions are listed on its My Community Hub. For caregivers of children under 18.

entries.name: Respite Services (Kerry's Place)
entries.description: Respite for families of autistic children, teens and adults in Ontario, so parents and caregivers get a break while their family member takes part in individualized activities. Includes children's and adult respite house programs, day and after-school respite groups, and children's respite flexible funding in some regions.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed on the respite page.
entries.evidence: Sometimes families and caregivers need to take a break and recharge to fully support the Autistic child or adult in their life.
entries.notes: Each respite program covers different regions (for example, the adult respite house serves Dufferin, Halton, Peel, Waterloo and Wellington). Register with Kerry's Place intake first.

entries.name: Family & Adult Support (Autism Nova Scotia)
entries.description: One-on-one support across Nova Scotia for parents and caregivers of autistic children and adults, and for autistic adults. The team helps with understanding the diagnosis process, finding programs and services, school transitions, respite and advocacy, with regional Autism Support Coordinators around the province.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.evidence: Our Family & Adult Support teams offer one-on-one support across the lifespan, including: understanding the diagnosis process, program & service navigation, transition to-and-from school, adult support, respite services, advocacy and much more.
entries.notes: The central office team covers HRM, with separate contacts for ages 18 and under and 18+; regional coordinators cover Annapolis Valley, Cape Breton, Cumberland, Pictou, South Shore, South West, Strait Area and Truro.

entries.name: Parent Support Group, Truro (Autism Nova Scotia)
entries.description: An informal peer support group in Truro for parents and other caregivers supporting a loved one with autism (ASD) of any age. Members share experiences, ask each other about current challenges and learn how others have found resources.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.evidence: The Parent support groups brings together parents and other caregivers who have the common, shared experience of supporting a loved one who has ASD.
entries.notes: Meets at the Truro address listed; contact the Truro Autism Support Coordinator (truro@autismns.ca) for dates.

entries.name: Respite Support & Navigation Services (Autism Nova Scotia)
entries.description: Helps families in Nova Scotia's central region find respite care: families join a respite database to connect with vetted independent respite providers, and get help with respite funding options, appeals and local programs. It serves families of people of any age with diverse support needs, including autism.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.evidence: Through Autism Nova Scotia, individuals and families can onboard Nova Scotia's central region respite database to connect with vetted independent respite providers and other respite resources
entries.notes: The database covers the central region and is not limited to autism. Contact the Respite Support Coordinator through Autism Nova Scotia's central office.

entries.name: Sip N' Connect, South Shore (Autism Nova Scotia)
entries.description: A parent-led group on Nova Scotia's South Shore that meets in person once a month for families and caregivers who have a person with autism in their life. It shares resources, hosts guest presenters and builds connections between families.
entries.cost_note: There is no cost to register.
entries.evidence: Sip N' Connect is a parent-led group that meets once a month. The group is for families and caregivers who have a person with autism in their life.
entries.notes: Hosted by Autism Nova Scotia's South Shore chapter (southshore@autismns.ca); the exact meeting place is not on the page.

entries.name: AutismBC Meets support groups (AutismBC)
entries.description: Monthly peer-led support groups on Zoom for parents and caregivers of autistic children and adults across BC, with groups for families new to autism, families going through transitions and those supporting an autistic adult. AutismBC also runs Meets for autistic adults.
entries.cost_note: AutismBC membership is free; no fee is listed for the groups.
entries.evidence: Our Meets are hosted virtually via Zoom by our Regional Coordinators and community members. These Meets are tailored for both caregivers of autistic individuals and autistic adults, covering the entire lifespan from birth to seniors.
entries.notes: Groups: New to Autism (3rd Tuesday), Transitions and Beyond (2nd Thursday and 4th Monday) and Supporting Adults (2nd Wednesday). A peer-led space, not a clinical or crisis service.

entries.name: Family Support (Autism Calgary)
entries.description: Autism Calgary's Family Support Team helps autistic people and their families in the Calgary area with autism questions, resources, finding service providers, and navigating healthcare, education and government funding such as FSCD. Families can email, call or come to drop-in hours, and newcomers can join a virtual New to Calgary / New Autism Diagnosis presentation.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.address: 3639 26 Street NE, Suite A, Calgary AB, T1Y 5E1
entries.evidence: Our Family Support Team provides support to Autistic individuals & their families. We offer information, resources, help finding services providers, help with navigating funding and more.
entries.notes: Office drop-in Monday to Thursday, 10am to 2pm (Mondays for FSCD questions, Wednesdays for autistic adult resources). The team does not provide therapy, respite, case management or financial support.

entries.name: Peer Support Groups (Autism Calgary)
entries.description: Free peer support groups in Calgary for parents and caregivers of autistic children and adults, including a monthly Parent to Parent Coffee Support at the Autism Calgary office, a Moms Coffee Support meet-up and the Keeping it Together (KIT) group for autism moms. There are also groups for autistic adults.
entries.cost_note: Autism Calgary says its peer support groups are free.
entries.address: 3639 26 Street NE, Suite A, Calgary AB, T1Y 5E1
entries.evidence: Autism Calgary offers FREE Peer Support Groups for parents, caregivers and Autistic individuals.
entries.notes: Groups are for registered adults only and childcare is not available; register before attending. Some groups also meet virtually.

entries.name: Parents of Autistic Adult Discussion Group (Autism Edmonton)
entries.description: A discussion group in Edmonton for parents and caregivers of autistic adults, to share experiences, get support and exchange ideas and information, often with guest speakers.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.evidence: This group is dedicated to fostering a community of parents and caregivers, creating a supportive network for those with adult autistic children.
entries.notes: Open only to parents of autistic adults; one of Autism Edmonton's drop-in groups run by its Support Services Team, with dates on its event calendar.

entries.name: CARES Caregiver Support Program (Autism Yukon)
entries.description: An eight-week Zoom group from Autism Yukon for parents and caregivers of children with complex needs, such as autistic children, that helps with the social, emotional and psychological challenges of caregiving and with looking after themselves.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.evidence: This eight week Zoom group is designed to address the social, emotional, and psychological challenges that caregivers of children with complex needs often face.
entries.notes: Contact Autism Yukon's navigator (navigator@autismyukon.org) about the next group. Autism Yukon also offers community navigation for families and self-advocates of all ages.

entries.name: Répit de fin de semaine, La Maisonnette (Autisme Montréal)
entries.description: Weekend respite at Autisme Montréal's respite house, La Maisonnette, for autistic children, teens and adults aged 5 and up, open every weekend from September to June. Families choose a full stay (Friday evening to Sunday) or a partial daytime stay, giving parents a break while participants take part in structured group activities.
entries.cost_note: $460 for a full weekend stay or $255 for a partial stay.
entries.evidence: La maison de répit d'Autisme Montréal ouvre ses portes chaque fin de semaine, de septembre à juin, aux personnes autistes de 5 ans et plus.
entries.notes: Pages are in French. Registration is by phone on set dates (winter 2027 registration opened October 26, 2026); one weekend per family per season, with 6 full-stay and 2 partial-stay places.

entries.name: Intervention familiale (Autisme Montréal)
entries.description: Listening, support and accompaniment for parents and families of autistic children and adults in Montreal, by phone or in person by appointment. Staff explain autism and how to get a diagnosis, financial help for parents of autistic children, therapies and public and private services, and help families who struggle to get services, including going with them to meetings.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.evidence: Autisme Montréal offre à tous les parents, étudiants, et professionnels un service d'aide et de renseignement sur l'autisme.
entries.notes: Pages are in French. The page has separate guidance for people living outside the Montreal area.

entries.name: Family Support Groups (Extend-A-Family Toronto)
entries.description: Support groups across Toronto for parents and guardians of children with developmental disabilities, including the Coffee and Chat Evening Parent Group and the Inclusive Education Parent Network for parents working toward inclusion in regular classrooms, plus a group for adult siblings.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.evidence: You are invited to join our gathering of parents and guardians of children with disabilities.
entries.notes: Pre-registration is required for every group, through the contact person listed for each. Extend-A-Family is funded by the Ontario Ministry of Children, Community and Social Services.

entries.name: Support Program (FASD Network of Saskatchewan)
entries.description: One-on-one support in Saskatchewan for people with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD) and their families and caregivers. Support Workers help with strategies for living with FASD, referrals, advocacy, getting a diagnosis or assessment, and navigating school, health, income support, social services and justice systems.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.evidence: Through our Support Program, we provide services to give individuals and families direct support in their daily lives.
entries.notes: No diagnosis is needed and there is no wait-list. Offices in Saskatoon and Regina, plus a provincial support worker who travels or connects by phone and video.

entries.name: Parent Support Groups (Autism Manitoba)
entries.description: Parent support groups run by Autism Manitoba, which has helped families of autistic people in Manitoba since 1977. Parents sign up through the website to join the groups and get updates.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.address: Unit i - 3525 Roblin Boulevard, Winnipeg, Manitoba R3R 0C6, Canada
entries.evidence: Parent Support Groups - Sign Up for our Groups!
entries.notes: The page is only a sign-up form, with no schedule or locations, so a reviewer may want to confirm the groups are running. The old domain autismmanitoba.com now hosts an unrelated site; use autismmanitoba.ca.

entries.name: Family Support Groups (Autism Society of Newfoundland and Labrador)
entries.description: Parent-led support groups in Newfoundland and Labrador for parents and caregivers of autistic people, a place to share experiences, find resources and connect with other families. Current groups include ones in Bonavista, Glovertown and area, the Avalon and the Burin Peninsula, with ASNL Navigators helping arrange meeting spaces.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.evidence: Family Support Groups are inclusive and welcoming to parents and caregivers of autistic individuals, creating a safe space to share experiences, access resources, and build meaningful connections across families.
entries.notes: Groups are run by parents, so schedules are set by each group; some list their own contacts. ASNL has offices in St. John's, Clarenville, Corner Brook and Happy Valley-Goose Bay, and its Navigators help families find services.

entries.name: Parent/Caregiver Support Group (Autism Connections, Fredericton)
entries.description: A support group in Fredericton where parents, caregivers and other family members of autistic children and adults meet, chat and share their experiences of supporting a loved one with autism.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.address: 1666 Lincoln Road, Fredericton, New Brunswick E3B 8J6, Canada
entries.evidence: The parent/caregiver support group is a safe place for parents/caregivers/family members of autistic individuals to meet, chat, and share experiences of their families' journeys supporting a loved one with autism.
entries.notes: Autism Connections is a Fredericton charity that also runs skills programs, camps and counselling; the page does not give meeting dates, so contact them to join.

entries.name: PEERS® for Adolescents (Kerry's Place)
entries.description: The PEERS® social skills group program for autistic teens aged 13 to 17 in Ontario who want to learn and practise the social skills for making and keeping friends, using strategies for different social situations. Parents and family members attend their own education sessions to help their teen.
entries.cost_note: Listed as Ontario Autism Program (OAP) eligible; no fee shown.
entries.evidence: The Program for the Education and Enrichment of Relational Skills (PEERS®) is a group social intervention program for Autistic teens ages 13 – 17 who want to learn and practice the social skills connected with developing and maintaining friendships.
entries.notes: Requires an autism diagnosis; offered in Dufferin, Halton, Peel, Simcoe, Toronto, Waterloo, Wellington and York. Register with Kerry's Place intake first. Kerry's Place PEERS for Young Adults is already in ResourceHub.

entries.name: Social Group, Halifax (Autism Nova Scotia)
entries.description: Bi-weekly social groups in Halifax for autistic teens (13 to 17) and adults (18+) who want to meet autistic peers, make friends and practise social and communication skills through movie nights, board games, community outings and dinners out.
entries.cost_note: No fee at registration; from fall 2026 each activity has a variable event fee paid online.
entries.evidence: Teen and Adult Social Groups bring together teens (13 years old and up) and adults who would like to meet autistic peers/peers with autism.
entries.notes: Runs Thursdays and Fridays; members sign up for monthly activities first-come, first-served after onboarding with the Recreation Coordinator.

entries.name: Supported Social Group, HRM (Autism Nova Scotia)
entries.description: A staff-led social group in Halifax for autistic teens and adults with higher support needs, who attend with a support person (not a parent) and meet every two weeks to make friends through arts and crafts, games and short outings.
entries.cost_note: $80 registration fee per year (September 2026 to May 2027).
entries.evidence: The Supported Social Group is an environment where autistic teens and adults meet and socialize while being supported by a respite worker.
entries.notes: Teens meet Wednesdays 5:15 to 6:15 PM and adults 6:30 to 7:30 PM at Autism Nova Scotia's central office.

entries.name: AutismBC Socials (AutismBC)
entries.description: Members-only social clubs, online and in person, where autistic people in BC connect through shared interests such as Minecraft and Pokémon, build confidence and make friends with structured support.
entries.cost_note: AutismBC membership is free; club fees, if any, are not listed.
entries.evidence: AutismBC Socials provide fun, inclusive spaces where autistic individuals can connect, build confidence, and foster a sense of community.
entries.notes: Current clubs include a Minecraft Club and Pokémon clubs (one for juniors); programs are for registered AutismBC members.

entries.name: Teen Programs: Improv for Autism and Camp Connect (Autism Resource Centre, Regina)
entries.description: Social programs in Regina for autistic teens: Improv for Autism, a 10-week acting and improvisation class with the Globe Theatre that focuses on spontaneity and socializing, and Camp Connect, a camp for teens aged 13 to 18 that teaches social skills through themed activities and community outings.
entries.cost_note: Programs start with an ARC membership; fees are not listed on the page.
entries.evidence: Camp Connect is designed for autistic teens between the ages of 13-18 who are interested in meeting new people and trying different activities.
entries.notes: Camp Connect needs participants who can take part at a 1:3 staff ratio and have a functional form of communication.

entries.name: PEERS for Adolescents and PEERS for Young Adults (ASERT, University of Calgary)
entries.description: The PEERS social skills programs at the University of Calgary for autistic teens aged 13 to 18 and young adults aged 19 to 28 who want to learn how to make and keep friends. Parents or caregivers attend their own sessions to learn to coach their teen or young adult; ASERT also runs a friendship program (P4P) for autistic children aged 4 to 6.
entries.cost_note: $1250 for the whole program; bursaries may be available for PEERS-YA.
entries.evidence: PEERS and PEERS-YA are evidence-based and empirically-supported interventions designed to help motivated teens/adults learn how to make and keep friends.
entries.notes: For people with an autism spectrum disorder; weekly 1.5-hour sessions (14 for teens, 16 for young adults) at the University of Calgary, with a parent or caregiver at every session. Email to join the waitlist for pre-screening.

entries.name: Social Skills Groups (This World's Ours)
entries.description: Small social skills groups in Vancouver for autistic children and teens: a Sunday social group for ages 5 to 12 with cooking, arts and crafts, games and sensory activities at a 1:4 ratio, and a PEERS group for teens.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not listed on the page.
entries.evidence: Social Group is a program that allows incorporating tools to improve the relationship and social interaction with peers, while providing an opportunity to meet other children
entries.notes: The teen PEERS group takes rolling applications; its details are only in a poster image on the page, so confirm dates and fees directly.

entries.name: Activités TSA sans DI (Autisme Montréal)
entries.description: Recreational, cultural and social activities in Montreal for independent autistic adults and older teens (16 and up) without an intellectual disability. Participants are Autisme Montréal members and meet a staff member before joining.
entries.cost_note: Autisme Montréal membership of $30 a year is required.
entries.evidence: Autisme Montréal organise plusieurs activités ludiques, culturelles et de socialisation.
entries.notes: Pages are in French. Contact the activities coordinator at ext. 3121; a leaflet of current adult activities is linked on the page.

entries.name: I CAN Centre for Assistive Technology (Glenrose Rehabilitation Hospital)
entries.description: An assistive technology clinic at the Glenrose Rehabilitation Hospital in Edmonton for children and adults with disabilities, including augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) such as speech-generating communication devices. After an intake meeting (usually on Zoom) and one or two in-person visits, the team assesses language, vision and physical skills, recommends technology and trains the person, family and community team, with a device loan library and technical support.
entries.cost_note: No fee for the service; families may pay for all or part of recommended equipment (AADL, NIHB or private insurance may help).
entries.evidence: Examples of how assistive technology can be used during daily activities, include managing the telephone, using a wheelchair to get around at home and in the community, using speech-generating communication devices to communicate with others
entries.notes: Separate adult and pediatric services, each with a Request for Services form. Located on Level 0 of the GlenEast Building; its pages link to the Alberta Aids to Daily Living speech generating communication device benefit.

entries.name: Communication Devices Program (Deer Lodge Centre)
entries.description: A Manitoba government-funded program at Deer Lodge Centre in Winnipeg that makes speech generating devices (SGDs) for augmentative and alternative communication available and affordable to eligible adults with severe communication disorders anywhere in Manitoba, renting devices at low cost.
entries.cost_note: Devices are rented to clients at a low cost.
entries.evidence: The Communication Devices Program (CDP) is mandated to ensure Speech Generating Devices (SGDs) are available and affordable to all eligible adults in the Province of Manitoba.
entries.notes: Serves clients in over 200 Manitoba communities; office hours Monday to Friday, 8 to 4, call ahead. Part of the Winnipeg Regional Health Authority's Assistive Technology Products and Services program.

entries.name: Augmentative & Alternative Communication Program (School of Communication Sciences and Disorders, Dalhousie University)
entries.description: A university group program in Halifax for teens and adults who communicate mainly with an AAC system (a computer, tablet or communication book) rather than speech. Led by a certified speech-language pathologist with graduate students, it builds vocabulary and independent communication through supported conversation and gives peer support.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.address: Sir Charles Tupper Medical Building 5850 College Street 2nd Floor, Room 2C01 PO Box 15000 Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada B3H 4R2
entries.evidence: The Augmentative & Alternative Communication (AAC) Program provides group treatment for adolescents and adults whose primary mode of communication is not speech.
entries.notes: Self-referral or referral from a speech-language pathologist or other provider in Nova Scotia or PEI; participants need an established AAC system and go through an evaluation. Meets on Fridays.

entries.name: Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) Program, Centre de réadaptation Marie Enfant (CHU Sainte-Justine)
entries.description: A specialized AAC program at the Marie Enfant Rehabilitation Centre in Montreal for children and teens under 18 in Quebec whose speech or language impairment, linked to a motor, sensory or developmental disorder, limits everyday communication. It assesses and recommends communication aids, and is the designated resource centre for Quebec's PMATCOM communication aids program.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed.
entries.address: 5200 Bélanger Street East Montreal, QC H1T 1C9
entries.evidence: Thus, the Augmentative and Alternative Communication Program provides children and teenagers who have speech or language impairments with alternative means to communicate.
entries.notes: Families cannot self-refer: the regional rehabilitation centre that coordinates the child's service plan (PSI) makes the referral. The contact page was last updated in 2023.

entries.name: Communication aids (Assistive Devices Program, Ontario)
entries.description: Ontario's Assistive Devices Program helps pay for communication aids, including speech-generating devices and other augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) systems, for people of any age with a long-term disability who cannot speak or whose speech is very hard to understand. A doctor or nurse practitioner refers you to an ADP-registered speech-language pathologist or occupational therapist, who may refer you on to an ADP communications clinic.
entries.cost_note: ADP pays 75% of the approved price and you pay 25% (100% for people on ODSP or Assistance for Children with Severe Disabilities); income is not considered.
entries.address: 5700 Yonge Street, 7th Floor Toronto, Ontario M2M 4K5
entries.evidence: Through the Assistive Devices Program (ADP), we help cover the cost of:
entries.notes: Needs a valid Ontario health card. The general ADP page (all device types) is already in ResourceHub; this page is specific to communication aids.

entries.name: Augmentative and alternative communication, Communication and Writing Aids Service (Holland Bloorview Kids Rehabilitation Hospital)
entries.description: A hospital AAC clinic in Toronto for children and youth whose speech does not meet their daily communication needs. Speech-language pathologists, occupational therapists and assistive technology consultants assess, set goals and train children and families in augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) tools and strategies, at the hospital, at home and in the community, and can authorize Assistive Devices Program funding.
entries.cost_note: No fees are listed; clinicians can authorize ADP funding for eligible clients.
entries.address: 150 Kilgour Road, Toronto Ontario Canada M4G 1R8
entries.evidence: The augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) stream serves children and youth whose speech does not meet their daily communication needs, and who require tools and strategies to support their face-to-face and written communication.
entries.notes: Needs a referral from a physician, nurse practitioner, speech-language pathologist, occupational therapist, physiotherapist or psychologist, then a screening call with the caregiver. Virtual appointments are possible.

entries.name: CAYA: Communication Assistance for Youth and Adults (BC)
entries.description: A province-wide BC program, funded by the Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction, that provides augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) systems and professional support to adults 19 and older whose speech does not meet their daily needs because of a severe communication disability.
entries.cost_note: Government-funded; the site does not state fees.
entries.evidence: Communication Assistance for Youth and Adults (CAYA) is a province-wide service program that supports adults aged 19 years and older who require an augmentative/alternative communication (AAC) system due to a severe communication disability
entries.notes: Needs a valid BC Personal Health Number and a Request for Service; there is a wait list, with three intake cycles a year triaged by urgency. Staff visit clients across BC, clustering visits to remote regions.

entries.name: Augmentative Communication and Educational Technology Service (ACETS), Alberta Children's Hospital
entries.description: An Alberta Health Services AAC assessment centre at the Alberta Children's Hospital in Calgary for children and adults who cannot meet their daily communication needs through speech, writing or computer access. It assesses and recommends augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) tools, strategies and alternate access, and assesses eligibility for Alberta Aids to Daily Living funding for speech generating communication devices.
entries.cost_note: No fee for the service itself; clients may pay for all or part of any recommended equipment.
entries.evidence: Provides assessment and consultation services to children and adults who experience verbal and / or written communication difficulties.
entries.notes: A health care provider refers through the Alberta Referral Directory; clients need an active community therapy team and to have tried low-tech strategies first. ACETS does not act as the primary therapy team.

entries.name: Augmentative and Alternative Communication Clinic (West Park Healthcare Centre, UHN)
entries.description: An adult AAC clinic in Toronto that assesses and recommends augmentative and alternative communication methods and devices for adults (18+) whose disability affects face-to-face or written communication, and supports people who lease their communication systems.
entries.cost_note: No fee for assessment or consultation with a valid OHIP card; buying or leasing a system is paid by the client, who may be eligible for ADP.
entries.evidence: Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) refers to methods that either supplement or replace an individual's speech and/or writing.
entries.notes: Eligible: adults who are past or present West Park patients, or outpatients from anywhere in Ontario with a congenital physical disability affecting communication, so many autistic adults would not qualify. Online referral form or Intake Inquiry Line ext. 34679.

entries.name: Sarang Kitchen
entries.description: A halal Korean fried chicken restaurant and bar in Toronto whose founders set out to welcome neurodivergent guests. Its own pages describe sensory-friendly hours daily before 9 pm with calming music and reduced lighting, sensory boxes with fidgets, weighted blankets and noise-cancelling headphones, and a multi-sensory room for guests who feel overstimulated or anxious.
entries.cost_note: A restaurant; guests pay menu prices.
entries.evidence: Our sensory boxes and multi-sensory room allow guests to dine in our restaurant at ease knowing that there are fidgets, weighted blankets, and noise-cancelling headphones they can use
entries.notes: Two Toronto locations, but the site gives conflicting addresses (footer: 1056 Bloor St W and 774 Danforth Ave; catering page: 2450 Bloor St W and 703 Danforth Ave) and doesn't say which location has the sensory room. The phone is the one listed for Bloor.

entries.name: Family Connections (The Sashbear Foundation)
entries.description: A free group program (24 hours in total) for parents, partners, other family members and friends of someone with emotion dysregulation, including borderline personality disorder (BPD). Trained peer family members teach skills based on dialectical behaviour therapy (DBT) for coping, relationships and communication, online across Canada in English and French.
entries.cost_note: Provided free of charge to participants.
entries.evidence: Family ConnectionsTM (FC) is an evidence-based 24-hour group program for people who are in a relationship with someone who has emotion dysregulation or related problems.
entries.notes: All groups currently run on Zoom; French groups are listed on Sashbear's French website. Sashbear is based in Toronto.

entries.name: Virtual Parent Support Groups (CADDAC)
entries.description: Free monthly drop-in support groups on Zoom for parents and caregivers of children with ADHD anywhere in Canada, led by CADDAC-trained facilitators who are parents of children with ADHD themselves. Parents share their stories and strategies with others who understand.
entries.cost_note: Listed as free.
entries.evidence: Who can join: Open to any parents/caregivers of children with ADHD in Canada. All support groups are drop-in.
entries.notes: Two groups: the 4th Monday of each month at 7:00pm ET, and a Tuesday group (previously Thursday). Participants read CADDAC's ground rules before registering.

entries.name: Understanding Your Child's ADHD (CADDAC)
entries.description: A three-week introductory program on Zoom for parents and caregivers of a child newly diagnosed with ADHD or flagged for possible ADHD at school. It covers what ADHD is, how it affects the child and family at home and at school, IEPs and practical strategies, with time to share experiences with other parents.
entries.cost_note: $30 plus HST.
entries.evidence: This 3-week program is meant to be a first step for parents with a newly diagnosed child or for those who's child has been flagged for possible ADHD at school.
entries.notes: Runs several times a year (the next starts November 10, 2026, Tuesdays at 8pm ET); sessions are not recorded and need active participation.

entries.name: ISAAC Canada (International Society for Augmentative and Alternative Communication)
entries.description: The Canadian chapter of the international society for augmentative and alternative communication (AAC), for people with complex communication needs, their families and professionals. It shares AAC awareness resources (including a list of AAC camps in Canada), runs Breaking the ICE conferences and offers membership with a newsletter.
entries.cost_note: Membership benefits are listed; fees are not shown on the pages checked.
entries.address: 312 Dolomite Drive Suite 216 Toronto, ON M3J 2N2
entries.evidence: ISAAC Canada's mission is to promote the best possible communication for people with complex communication needs.
entries.notes: Mainly a membership and awareness association, not a clinic; useful for families looking for AAC community and events. Membership benefits are aimed largely at professionals.

entries.name: Autcraft
entries.description: An online Minecraft (Java Edition) server and community for autistic children and their families, also open to autistic adults, with players from around the world. Players register and are whitelisted, chat is in English and staff monitor the server 24/7.
entries.cost_note: No joining fee is stated; players need Minecraft Java Edition. The site has a store and takes donations.
entries.evidence: Autcraft is the first Minecraft server dedicated to providing a safe, fun, and learning environment for children with autism and their families.
entries.notes: Active as of October 2026 (news posts that month and players online). Registration asks for a parent's contact details for players under 18; whitelisting can take a few days to two weeks. The info page (autcraft.info) is linked from the site's footer.
